newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Nov 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Nov 25.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on November 25. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Indonesia will be given priority in oil exploration and exploitation contracts in the semi-autonomous southern Philippines region of Mindanao, Aburizal Bakrie, head of Indonesia's Chamber of Commerce, said. The comments came after a weekend meeting with Nur Misuari, governer of Mindanao.

Indonesian non-governmental organisations (NGOs) have called for the banning of television advertisements which insult the dignity of women. One such advertisement shows a man who repeatedly goes out at night because his wife has lost her sexual appeal. Only after she takes the advertised herbal medicine does she regain her youthful good looks.

Abdurrahman Wahid, leader of the 30-million strong Islamic Nahdlatul Ulama, has been invited to accompany Nobel laureate Bishop Carlos Belo when he attends the Nobel ceremony in Norway to receive his prize for promoting peace in East Timor.

Around 1,250 Indonesian traders were badly hit by a huge fire in Senen, Jakarta on Friday night. The blaze, which started at around midnight due to faulty electrical wiring, devastated an entire shopping plaza.
